hoi4_general_trait.description: Live-verified (pp13, 17 Nov 2026: a list and an assignment): give an own army general an assignable trait for command power (NDefines UNIT_LEADER_ASSIGN_TRAIT_COST, read from the game's defines; 15 in 1.19.4) with the game's own trait tree window: the card's trait button when the general leads an army or army group, else an own army's panel, its commander list and the general's Traits button; then the trait's entry in the tree. `general` is the name hoi4_commanders lists; `trait` is an assignable trait's script key or localised name (from common/unit_leader, so mods work); without `trait` the first trait the tree lets the general pick is taken, the earliest of `prefer` (keys or names) first. list:true opens the tree and returns every entry (name, script key, assignable, state owned/available/locked, can_pick), the free trait slots shown, command power and the cost, changing nothing. Typed refusals before input: unknown_commander (closest names), trait_unknown, trait_not_assignable (a trait the game grants), insufficient_command_power ("costs N command power and M are held"), catalog_unavailable; from the window before the click: no_own_army, general_not_listed, wrong_leader, trait_not_offered (lists the tree), trait_owned, trait_unavailable, no_free_trait_slot, no_enabled_trait, trait_not_visible. Verified by the entry turning to the owned state, else by command power dropping by about the cost.

hoi4_industry.description: Own civilian, military and dockyard factory counts (validated against the top bar total) and political power; consumer goods share, output modifier, trade-civilian usage, exact stability, war support and PP daily gain are null with reasons. Pure read.

hoi4_input_geometry.description: Read-only own GUI dimensions and scale diagnostics. Mac-only include_source_point adds witnessed cached ordinary SDL coordinates joined to the owned window; defaults off. No current event/frame, hit routing or input authorization.

hoi4_input_lease.description: Exclusive configured-controller lease for ordinary macOS input. Acquire uses holder; renew/release use only lease_token. Status takes only op. Observations do not need a lease.

hoi4_intelligence.description: Own intelligence agency, read-only (no input, no lease, never pauses). Returns the agency name (validated live: Abwehr for Germany), the 5 upgrade branches with their upgrades from the loaded database joined with the install's scripts (levels, factory use during progress, prerequisite upgrades, per-level modifiers), the operative mission keys, the agency defines (creation/upgrade days and factories) and, with include_operations:true, the operations catalogue (operatives, network strength, days, risk). Live state from game memory (macOS 1.19.4.1): agency created/creating, upgrade levels and the running upgrade, operative slots, offered candidates, the recruited operatives with their mission, target and operation, intel network strength per target and state, and operations_running (operation, target, operatives at work, auto commence). A part that cannot be read on this build is reported as state_read:false with the error rather than guessed.

hoi4_map_daynight.description: Turn the map's day/night shading off (on:false, the default) or on: the game starts every session with it on, and at night the map is dark, so units, fronts and state colours are hard to read. One click on the toggle in the bottom-right map controls; the result is read back from the map's brightness (shading off brightens a map in night). In daylight nothing changes on screen: the result says no_visible_change, and the call is best made when the map shows night. A view change only.

hoi4_map_mode.description: Switch the map mode with the game's own F-key shortcut, as a human checks the map: political (F1, default; armies and fronts), naval (F2), air (F3, air regions and superiority), supply (F4), terrain (F5), resistance (F6), compliance (F7), resources (F8), air_raids (F9), factions (F10). A view change only (no game state changes, nothing to read back): switch to political again before giving army orders. Look at a mode when its domain matters: supply before an offensive, resistance and compliance for occupied states, air for superiority, naval for sea lanes.

hoi4_mio_design_team.description: Browse only, assigns nothing (live pp4, 17 Nov 2026): the politics view's organisation slots open a roster to look at; the game assigns an organisation from a task (a production line: hoi4_mio_line; a technology; a design). Kept for older plans: put a military-industrial organisation into a design-team slot of the politics view: Q politics view, the slot's roster button (the `slot`-th shown organisation slot, default 0), the organisation's row in the list (found by its localised name; `organization` is the script key from hoi4_mios, e.g. GER_porsche_organization). Typed refusals: organization_unknown, organization_not_allowed (allowed block rules the tag out) before input; mio_system_absent (the politics view shows no organisation slot: the organisation system is not in use in this game, designers are ideas, use hoi4_politics_choose), slot_unknown, organization_not_offered (lists the rows) found from the windows before the first state-changing click. Verified only by the list closing (political power before/after is recorded): verification gui_only. Results carry validated:false.

hoi4_mio_line.description: Attach an organisation to an own production line with ordinary input, or read the line's state. The production line's organisation button (drawn at scale 0.45 in its rect's bottom-left corner) opens the roster of the organisations that make that equipment, under a 'Produce without a Military Industrial Organization' entry; its rows are read from memory (name, organisation or not) before any row click, the list is wheeled to its top, read again, and only an organisation row drawn in full is clicked (live pp14, 17 Nov 2026: Rheinmetall attached to a new anti-air line). The last line, whose button the screen edge cuts, is moved to the top for the roster and back to the bottom after. `organization` (localised name or key) picks the row, else the first organisation offered. A line that has an organisation answers assigned, already_attached without input. list:true opens the roster, answers attached and offered (the organisations' names) and closes it, changing nothing. Verified from the line's own row (has_mio_background). A line costs no political power. The politics view's organisation slots only browse rosters. The line is addressed like hoi4_production_set (line = entry_index from hoi4_production_lines, with its equipment). Typed refusals: invalid_target, organization_unknown, organization_not_allowed (before input); line_takes_no_organization (no organisation makes the equipment: the line shows no button, its button is disabled, or its roster offers only the 'Produce without' row); organization_not_offered (the roster's organisations named); row_not_visible (the row is below the five drawn in full); roster_unreadable (the roster's layout is not the reviewed one).

hoi4_mio_policy.description: UNVALIDATED (no live test yet): attach a policy to an organisation: politics view, the slot's roster, the organisation's details button, Open policies, the policy row (by localised name). `organization` and `policy` are script keys (mio_policy_general_ruthless_contracts, ...). Typed refusals: organization_unknown, organization_not_allowed, policy_unknown (before input); mio_system_absent, slot_unknown, organization_not_offered, policy_not_offered (lists the rows) from the windows before the click. Verified from the detail window's attached policy name only (verification gui_only). Results carry validated:false.

hoi4_mio_trait.description: Live-verified (6 Nov 2026 on 1.19.4 with 10 DLCs: a trait queued, read back by reopening the detail window): queue a trait of an organisation's trait tree: politics view, the slot's roster, the organisation's details button, the trait icon at `trait_index` (0-based in the order the tree window lists its entries; trait entries carry no text, so call with list:true first: it returns each entry's index, enabled state, queue number and whether it is visible, changing nothing). Exactly one of trait_index and list. Typed refusals: organization_unknown, organization_not_allowed (before input); mio_system_absent, slot_unknown, organization_not_offered, trait_unknown, trait_already_queued, trait_unavailable, trait_not_visible from the windows before the click. Verified from the entry's queue number only (verification gui_only). Results carry validated:false.

auto.description: in the same visit, queue the first open (enabled, visible, not held) traits until this many enabled traits wait in the queue; with trait_indices they come after those

trait_indices.description: several traits queued in order in ONE visit of the tree window (the game's completion queue unlocks them as points come); each read back from its queue number; an already queued trait counts as reached; refused ones are listed in the receipt (unchanged)

hoi4_mios.description: Military-industrial organisations and designers for the own country, read-only (no input, no lease, never pauses). Reports the own active designer ideas (validated live: e.g. GER_daimler_benz), the organisation catalogue of the install for the own tag (key, category land/naval/air, equipment, research categories, trait count, icon, matching designer idea; allowed_for_tag is true/false/null when it depends on DLC or flags) and the memory template count. Per-organisation state (size, funds, unlocked traits, policy, design team, production lines) is NOT mapped on this build state and is reported unavailable (mio_system.state_read:false). tag overrides the catalogue's tag; include_all lists every organisation script.

hoi4_naval_invasion.description: UNVALIDATED (no live test yet): Order ONE naval invasion of an enemy coastal state for land units: the army's card selects it (or a box selection takes exactly the named `divisions` standing in one state), the battle plan toolbar's naval invasion button (with_harbor:true picks the harbour variant), a left click on the source state's centre, a right click on the destination state's centre, Return. One deliberate order per call, nothing is repeated. Aim: the Find view centres each state and the click goes to the centre plus an optional pixel offset ([dx,dy], within 350); a centre that is not a valid port or coast needs an offset. The game needs convoys, preparation days and naval dominance (read the army card). Typed refusals before input: own_state, enemy_required (the state's owner or controller is not at war with us), not_coastal, source_not_coastal, no_transports (no convoys), no_such_army, no_such_division, divisions_not_together, divisions_not_isolated, army_location_unknown, invalid_target; while driving selection_mismatch, button_disabled, input_readback_failed (the drawing is cancelled with Escape). Verified by more battle plan orders on the army or divisions heading for a province of the state. Result has validated:false.

hoi4_naval_production_options.description: Read-only (memory, no input): the ship and convoy designs the Production panel can build (not decommissioned) with their equipment keys and existing lines, and the own naval production lines with their line index and dockyard count; each design and line says whether it builds convoys (`convoy`). Use the equipment key and optional design id with hoi4_production_add; ship and convoy lines are added through the Production panel's naval category.

hoi4_navy_ui.description: DEBUG ONLY (never listed to a player): dump the naval UI tree or send one ordinary input.

hoi4_observe.description: What changed since your last look, from the server's watcher (it samples your own situation a few times a second): typed changes with a sequence number (event_opened, own_state_lost, war_started, army_moved, army_organisation_low, army_supply_low, army_plan_stopped, army_gone, alert_raised, research_slot_idle, focus_finished, peace_conference_opened ...; urgent ones marked) plus a short brief of now. Pass `since` = the `seq` of your previous reply; 0 gives the brief and the current seq. Optional kinds filter, urgent_only, limit. Pure read; answers at once even while an action runs.

hoi4_occupation.description: Read-only (memory, no input, no pause): resistance and compliance of occupied states (La Résistance). Per state: state_id, name, owner, controller, role (occupied_by_player, own_state_held_by_other, owned_non_core_or_resisting, other), resistance %, resistance target %, resistance speed %/day, compliance %, compliance speed %/day, plus unconfirmed extras (target before additions, target added from a neighbouring state). Also the player's occupation law key (unconfirmed slot). Default scope: states the player controls that have resistance or another owner, and own states others hold; scope all lists every occupied or resisting state in the world. Garrison strength and suppression are not read.

hoi4_occupation_law.description: Set the DEFAULT occupation law for all occupied territories (the Occupied Territories view's Territory Management law) with ordinary input: an occupied or resisting state's view, its occupation-law button, the default-law button, the law's row. Verified from the country's occupation law in memory (hoi4_occupation player_occupation_law). `law` is a key of the game's common/occupation_laws (mods included); hoi4_occupation `laws` lists them in the list's order with whether the game shows each to you (its visible trigger: ideology, tag, DLC). The row is found from the laws shown above it: refused before any input with law_not_shown (the game hides it from you) or law_row_unknown (a visible trigger on that row or above it reads something no tool reads yet, such as another country, a flag or a focus; the ruling ideology is taken from the country's history). Harsher laws cut resistance and raise the garrison need; milder ones raise compliance slowly and need fewer garrison troops. A law the game disables for you is not applied: the readback refuses it with action_not_applied. `via_state` is an occupied or resisting state id (default: the first one hoi4_occupation lists). `state` (the law of that one state, not the default) is not yet built: refused with not_yet_built.

hoi4_officer_corps.description: Live-verified read (pp18, pp23, 17 Nov 2026) and pick (fk1, 18 Nov 2026: army:0, army:1, army:2, air:0): the officer corps spirits with ordinary input. list:true opens the officer corps view (Shift+E), returns its spirit slots (view army/navy/air, index, entry kind such as academy, army or division_command, the slot button's rect, selected, taken: a spirit shown in the slot) and closes it, changing nothing. With slot "VIEW:INDEX" (e.g. "army:0") it also opens that slot's spirit window and returns its title and the spirits offered (index, name, cost in the branch's experience, entry rect); the window closes with the view. With slot and spirit (a name the window shows) it picks that spirit: clicks its entry and verifies the slot shows a spirit it did not show before (taken_before/taken_after; Diverged otherwise, e.g. too little experience). Refusals while driving: slot_missing, spirit_unknown (lists the spirits offered). Results carry verification gui_only.

hoi4_operation_start.description: Prepare an intelligence operation against a target with ordinary input, as a player does: agency view (Shift+W), Operations tab, the operation's row (scrolled into view; one row per target with a network, the opened window's memory must name the asked operation and target), Prepare, one free operative per slot picked by name in the game's list, optionally Commence when ready, then the window's Prepare. The game then gathers the equipment and civilian factories and, with auto_commence (default true), commences on its own; the operation's phases then run for its days. Refusals before input: unknown_operation, operation_picks_location (the operation also picks a state or region in its window, e.g. coup, sabotage, coordinated strike: not built), agency_not_created, operative_unknown, operative_busy, not_enough_operatives (from memory and the content's files); from the windows before the first state-changing click: operation_unavailable (the game disables Prepare), operation_not_listed, operative_slots_unavailable, operative_not_offered, operative_pick_failed. Live-verified on 1.19.4 (collaboration government, ITA on ETH, at war). Use hoi4_operations first: it lists every missing piece with a code. Verified from memory: the operation appears among the agency's operations (hoi4_intelligence operations). operatives = recruited positions (hoi4_intelligence operatives.list order); default the first free ones.

hoi4_operations.description: Read-only: intelligence operations against a target and whether each can be prepared now, decided without opening the agency. Definitions come from the running game's content (common/operations and common/operation_phases with mods layered): days, network strength, operatives, equipment and civilian factories, required and awarded tokens, allowed targets and the phase choices with their extra costs. Each operation is judged against the own state read from memory (network strength in the target = its strongest covered state, recruited operatives not on an operation, collaboration, ruling ideology and its rules, wars, the equipment stockpile, the install's DLCs): verdict.visible and verdict.ready are true | false | unknown; false lists every failing piece with a code (network_too_weak, not_enough_operatives, missing_token, not_allowed, unavailable, requirements_unmet, not_visible, not_a_target); waits_for lists equipment the stockpile lacks now (missing_equipment: Prepare still works and the preparation takes it as it arrives, so it delays the commencement); unknown names the triggers the server cannot read (flags, focuses, national coverage, other countries' affairs). target = a tag (default: every country with an own network); operations = keys to judge; include_hidden lists operations whose visible conditions fail. No input, no lease, never pauses.

hoi4_operative_assign.description: Send a recruited operative (`operative` = 0-based position among the recruited ones on the operative bar) on a mission: portrait, the order bar's mission button, then one click on the target. State missions (build_intel_network, quiet_intel_network, root_out_resistance) take `state_id`; country missions (counter_intelligence, control_trade, diplomatic_pressure, propaganda) take `country` (a tag; the Find view centres its lowest state id and that click picks the country; counter_intelligence without country starts at home with a right click). boost_ideology (needs the ideology window) and `operation` refuse with mission_not_built / operation_not_built (operations are started with hoi4_operation_start). Typed refusals before input: invalid_arguments, target_required, country_has_no_states, unknown_country; agency_not_created, operative_unknown, operative_busy (on an operation), already_on_mission from memory; operative_bar_unavailable, mission_unavailable (the game disables the button) from the windows. Verified by memory (mission and target). Live-verified on 1.19.4.

hoi4_operative_recruit.description: Recruit an operative into a free slot of the operative bar: Shift+W agency view, the empty slot, then the candidate `candidate` (0-based index into hoi4_intelligence's candidate list, default 0), picked in the recruitment window by its name. Typed refusals before input, from memory: agency_not_created, no_free_operative_slot, operative_slot_locked (says in how many days candidates are offered: AGENCY_OPERATIVE_RECRUITMENT_TIME counts from creation), unknown_candidate; candidate_not_shown and operative_bar_unavailable from the window. Verified by memory: Reached when the operative count grew, Diverged when someone else was recruited. Live-verified on 1.19.4.

hoi4_overview.description: Fresh owned-country process snapshot. Pure bounded reads; never pauses.

hoi4_peace_exit.description: Leave the peace conference (the Confirm and Exit / done button and the OK of its confirmation); accepted bids persist. Refused before input with exit_not_available or no_conference_open. Verified when the conference window closes. validated:false.

hoi4_peace_options.description: Read the open peace conference from its window: header (current player, own remaining points = current_score, world tension, bidding phase, turn), which controls are usable (demand kinds take_state/liberate/puppet/force_government/take_navy, end turn, done), participant, available-action and bid lists as the window shows them, and for the asked `states` their owner and occupier. Costs are not stored: a state's tooltip shows them and hoi4_peace_take reports each state's cost as the score drop. No lease, no input. validated:false (no conference was arranged live; procedure in docs/PLAYBOOK_TOOL_GAPS.md).

hoi4_peace_status.description: Read-only: whether the peace conference window is open and, when it is, the texts it shows (current player, score, bidding phase, turns left). Without a conference it returns the route an ordinary player takes (actions list, states on the conference map, End turn). NOT validated live while a conference is open (no war was fought in the qualification game); no peace action tool exists yet.

hoi4_peace_submit.description: Submit Demands for the round (the conference's end-turn button; one submission per round under the blind-bid rules). Refused before input with round_not_ready or no_conference_open. Verified when the header (phase, turn, score of the turn) changes or the window closes. validated:false.

hoi4_peace_take.description: In the open peace conference, choose the demand kind (default Take State; puppet:true = Puppet; release:true = Liberate) and add each listed state from the conference's own state list (country rows expand into state rows; Find and a map click as fallback), verifying each through the drop of the window's score; reports each state's cost. Refusals before input: no_conference_open, round_not_ready, action_not_available, unknown_state, state_not_offered (own state), cost_exceeds_points. `max_cost` stops after a state dearer than it. Nothing is submitted. validated:false. `force_government` (the force-government demand on the country owning the state) is not yet built: refused with not_yet_built.

hoi4_plan.description: Read or change the standing plan (plan.json in the run directory): research priorities, focus path, construction, training, production, politics, decisions. {op:get} returns it; {op:set, plan:{...}} merges the given keys (null removes a key); {op:request_revision, reason} asks for a revised plan (written to the change feed as revision_requested; the plan in force stays until plan_revised). hoi4_plan_run carries it out.

hoi4_plan_run.description: Carry out the standing plan for up to `seconds` (default 60): answer news and single-option events, fill empty research slots and the focus slot from the plan's lists, make planned politics picks and decisions, keep the training queue, put idle military factories on the priority lines and spend idle civilian factories on planned construction. Every step is an ordinary verified action under the given lease; the game is never paused. Returns early when a choice event needs the model or a peace conference opens. Use it instead of hoi4_wait_for while nothing else needs attention.

hoi4_politics_choose.description: Take an idea (law, advisor, designer) for one politics slot with ordinary input; verified when the slot holds the idea in memory. Refuses ideas the game disables. Same category/slot numbering as hoi4_politics_options (military_staff: 0 chief of army, 1 chief of navy, 2 chief of air force, 3-5 high command; research_production: 5 theorist); the idea must be one the slot offers, so use a slot of the idea's own kind.

hoi4_politics_options.description: List the ideas offered for one politics slot (opens the slot's selection window and closes it again; changes nothing). category: government (slots 0 mobilization law, 1 trade law, 2 economy law, 3-5 political advisors), research_production (slots 0 tank, 1 naval, 2 aircraft and 3 materiel designer, 4 industrial concern, 5 theorist; with Arms Against Tyranny the designer slots hold Military Industrial Organizations: hoi4_mio_* tools) or military_staff (slots 0 chief of army, 1 chief of navy, 2 chief of air force, 3-5 high command). A slot index is the slot's position in its category, the order of the slot lines in the game's common/idea_tags (a mod can change it); an advisor is hired from a slot of its own kind, so a high command advisor needs slot 3, 4 or 5. Returns each idea key with the game's enabled state, the slot's current idea, and slots: every slot of the category with its index and what it holds now.

hoi4_production_add.description: Add one own military or naval production line for a base equipment type (e.g. infantry_equipment, artillery_equipment, light_tank_equipment, fighter_equipment) with ordinary input: production panel, category button, the design in the selection window, then +/- until the line requests the given factories. Verified from the own line collection. Refuses equipment with no producible design. Optional `design` (a design id or design name from hoi4_designs / hoi4_design_create, same equipment type) picks that exact variant in the selection window instead of the first listed one. Ship hulls (ship_hull_*) and convoys (convoy_*) are added through the naval category; see hoi4_naval_production_options. The line gets no military-industrial organisation (the design is Shift+clicked past the organisation chooser); `organization` (the organisation's script key, as hoi4_mios lists it) is not yet built: it is refused with not_yet_built before any input.

bulk.description: Factories by the game's Ctrl+Click (+5) and Shift+Click (+10) steps, each read back; a chord the game does not take falls back to single clicks. Off until its live probe passes.

hoi4_production_controls.description: Linux read-only preview: joins an exact own current production line_handle and base equipment_id to its production row, named one-factory add/subtract controls, ordinary callback and local blockers. Optional same-snapshot renderer geometry. Never opens a panel, moves the cursor, pauses or authorizes input. Full line collection is validated before reading UI. Factory buttons clamp to at least one and depend on keyboard modifiers. Live validation pending.

hoi4_production_lines.description: Fresh own equipment-line collection only, validated in full before paging; default page 32. Exact Military/Naval snapshot-scoped opaque handles and signed active/damaged/requested factory counters. Unsupported types are metadata only, ownership unproved; completeness describes this collection's type coverage. Known owned lines can expose a base equipment type key after fresh canonical membership and variant/type checks; explicit unavailability covers unreviewed types. Custom variant identity, general production, allocation/idle capacity, eligibility and input authority unavailable. Each line also has `output` (macOS build): unit_cost (IC per unit), ic_last_day (IC put in on the last daily tick), units_per_day, progress (0..1 of the unit in progress, a ship's completion) with progress_ic and days_to_next_unit, units_left (null = runs until stopped), and for military lines efficiency (percent, mean of the working factory slots), efficiency_min, efficiency_cap (the line's cap with country modifiers and its organisation bonus), efficiency_start (a new line's start) and at_cap. Naval lines have no efficiency. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_production_priority.description: Move an own production line in the production view's priority order (a line higher in the list gets resources and factories first, so shortages and lost factories hit the bottom lines): the line's arrows (increase_priority, decrease_priority), Shift+click for to:top or to:bottom. The line is addressed like hoi4_production_set (line = entry_index from hoi4_production_lines, with its equipment). Verified by the line's place in the view's list (receipt detail: place before and after, the shown order).

hoi4_production_set.description: factories 0 removes the line (its close button). Set the requested factories of an own production line, addressed by its entry_index and equipment_id from hoi4_production_lines, with the line's ordinary +/- buttons (bulk: Ctrl +5 and Shift +10 clicks); each click is verified from memory. 0 keeps the line with no factories.

bulk.description: Factories by the game's Ctrl+Click (+5) and Shift+Click (+10) steps, each read back; a chord the game does not take falls back to single clicks. Off until its live probe passes.

hoi4_production_shortages.description: Per production line (military and naval) the resources it was allocated per day and which of them are in deficit for the whole country. The efficiency penalty is null (not in memory). Pure read; validated:false.

hoi4_province_graph.description: Land provinces of the given states and the provinces each one touches, from the install's map files (provinces.bmp, definition.csv, history/states): per province its id, its state and its land neighbours; its terrain with the terrain's combat width, support width, attack modifier, movement cost and attrition (common/terrain), whether it is coastal, and the bunker levels its state history sets (forts_in_history: start or the dated block; live levels are not read here); per border (borders[]) the river that draws it (small or large, with the attack penalty of the river defines; touches = a river meets the border only at a point, estimate) and special crossings of adjacencies.csv (sea strait with the sea province, impassable, canal rule). Use it to see which provinces an objective can be attacked from and to find a way over land; who holds a province is in hoi4_states (a state id query lists its provinces with their controllers). Pure read; no lease, no game memory.

hoi4_railway_build.description: Queue ONE railway with the game's railway construction mode: Shift+Click on a start node (a supply hub, naval base or the capital; the game builds the shortest path re-using existing railways) and a click on the target province. Give the start as `from_province` or `from_state` (its supply hub or naval base from the map files) and the target as `to_province` or `to_state` (its supply hub, else its largest victory point). Both ends are checked live before any input: the start must be an own railway node now (a supply hub or naval base read from the game, or the capital) and both ends own-controlled. `from_nearest_node:true` replaces a missing start, or one that is no own node, with the own railway node the network already feeds (capital, port, hub with a railway) nearest to the target over own-controlled land (the game re-uses existing railways, so the line is the same); the result says start_replaced. `to_nearest_node:true` makes the target the own railway node nearest to the given province (a railway feeds a hub, the hub feeds the provinces around it; a railway to a plain province only helps as part of the way to a hub); the result says target_node_for_province. `leg:true` (with a start) lets the target lie beyond own control: the way from the start to the target over land is computed from the map files (railways of map/railways.txt preferred, as the game re-uses them) and the railway goes to the last province of its own-controlled run from the start, so a plan names the two ends and the railway follows the front one leg at a time; the result says leg_of; refusals leg_built (every province of the own part of the way already has a railway: the next leg waits for more land), railway_complete (the whole way has one) and no_way. The receipt is journaled under request_id (Verified when the own construction queue holds one more line or one more railway level; a retry of the same id settles, it never clicks again). Typed refusals before input: not_a_railway_node and end_not_controlled (both name the nearest own node), route_not_controlled (own-controlled land does not join the start and the target: names the states on the way the player does not control; with from_nearest_node:true the start is replaced by an own node the target reaches instead), no_node_reachable (no own node reaches the target over own land: use a port, trucks or a hub), no_node_in_state, province_not_in_state, unknown_state. railway_not_queued after the clicks means the game refused the path (often: it already stands or is queued at its highest level). Railways cost 170 per level (+130 per existing level) and are the way to carry supply from the capital to far fronts.

hoi4_research.description: Fresh own completed technology IDs with bounded pagination, and active raw research counters. Progress units, days remaining and eligibility remain unverified. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_research_category.description: Read-only exact public folder ID association with the current own research tree, named tab, dense selection index and ordinary callback. Optional raw Sprite diagnostics; no tab switch or input authorization.

hoi4_research_extras.description: Own research bonuses that the research panel only shows as tooltips, read from game memory (no input, no lease, never pauses): limited-use technology bonuses ('free research bonus': name, uses left, bonus as a fraction, categories), limited-use cost reductions, idea research bonuses, and technology-sharing faction membership. The ahead-of-time penalty, licenses and scientist rosters are not mapped (see the not_read block; scientists belong to hoi4_special_projects). Validated live against the focus and idea scripts of the owned game.

hoi4_research_folders.description: Fresh sorted exact installed public research-folder IDs for the verified Linux layout. Native macOS returns unsupported_platform before memory reads. Independent of open GUI; canonical keys only, with no aliases, eligibility, geometry or input authorization. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_research_node_detail.description: One exact own current technology key: complete current-record ownership checks, target-only raw renderer/hierarchy and own detail-state diagnostics. Unrelated GUI is outside scope; no client rectangle or input authorization.

hoi4_research_nodes.description: Current own-tree nodes joined to public technology keys and conditional ordinary-control diagnostics. Full model validated before prefix filtering/pagination; default page 25. Visibility, eligibility and click routing unavailable. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_research_slot_control.description: One own research slot by current array index: conditional ordinary callback binding and raw typed renderer diagnostics. Optional include_geometry adds bounded Sprite cache and typed hierarchy observations. No guessed Background name, coordinates or input authorization.

hoi4_research_start.description: Start an own technology in a research slot (an empty one, or a busy one with replace:true, which switches that slot to this technology; without `slot` the first empty slot is used) with ordinary input (research panel, slot, folder tab, tile, Research), each click located from the live GUI and each stage verified from memory; succeeds only when the slot holds the technology. Refuses researched (code already_researched), already-assigned or busy-slot targets before any input. A tile scrolled out of view is refused. Stable request_id; every request ends in a terminal receipt (action_unconfirmed: the effect was not observed and the request is closed; read the state again before sending a fresh one).

hoi4_research_ui.description: Bounded own research slot widgets, selected slot, canonical technology Info windows, named ordinary research button state and exact render diagnostics. No eligibility, hit routing or input authorization.

hoi4_resources.description: Own strategic resources per day from memory: for oil, aluminium, rubber, tungsten, steel, chromium and coal the gross produced, available_for_production, daily need of the production lines, balance, balance (= the Production view strip number) and shortage flag, the raw ten pool slots, plus fuel stock and capacity. Imports/exports and the shortage penalty percent are null with a reason (not identified). Pure read, no lease, never pauses; validated:false (see evidence).

hoi4_save.description: Save the running game with the game's own Save dialog (Escape, Save, Save) under the name the game proposes (country and date), overwriting a save of the same name, and verify that a save file was written in the run's userdata/save games. Use it at the end of a campaign segment so the next launch continues exactly from this point (no turns are replayed). The game stays paused if it was paused; a game that was running is unpaused again after the save (resumed:true).

hoi4_skill_list.description: Read-only: the saved skills (name, purpose, parameters, status active/stale/retired, runs that worked and failed, whether it can run on this game version and mod set) and the current mod set. No input. Example: {}

hoi4_skill_retire.description: Mark a saved skill retired (kept on disk, never run again) with the reason. Example: {"name": "open_caps_trade", "reason": "the mod removed this panel"}

hoi4_skill_run.description: Run a saved skill: checks it may run here (not retired or stale, learned on this game version and mod set unless revalidate:true), that its required windows and widgets are on screen (a missing one marks it stale and refuses), runs its steps through the ordinary tools with this lease, then its verify checks; the run is counted in the skill file. A skill with reversible:false needs confirm_irreversible:true. Typed refusals: skill_not_found, skill_refused, skill_stale, irreversible_needs_confirmation, invalid_arguments (a missing parameter); skill_step_failed names the step. Example: {"name": "open_caps_trade", "args": {}, "request_id": "r2", "lease_token": "..."}

hoi4_skill_save.description: Keep something that worked as a named skill (a plain JSON file in the learned/skills folder, one per skill, readable and editable): name, purpose, parameters, the windows/widgets that must be on screen before it starts (requires), its steps (tool calls; "{param}" in a string is replaced by the run's argument; leave out request_id and lease_token), the proofs that it worked (verify), cost and whether one click can undo it (reversible). The game version and mod set are stamped on it. Refused with what to fix: invalid_skill; skill_exists (replace:true overwrites). Example: {"skill": {"name": "open_caps_trade", "purpose": "Open the mod's caps trade panel", "steps": [{"tool": "hoi4_ui_act", "args": {"widget": "topbar/caps_button"}}], "verify": [{"check": "window_opens", "id": "caps_window"}], "cost": "nothing", "reversible": true}}

hoi4_skill_show.description: Read-only: one saved skill in full (steps, requires, verify, cost, where it was learned, its runs) and why it cannot run here if it cannot. Example: {"name": "open_caps_trade"}

hoi4_special_project_assign.description: Put a scientist and/or a project into one own research facility with ordinary input: Research panel (W), Experimental Facilities tab, the facility card's scientist portrait and the roster row, then the facility icon, the project entry and Start. Give scientist (name as listed by hoi4_special_projects) and/or project (key, e.g. sp_air_radar); a project needs a scientist already in the facility or passed together. Verified from memory when the facility's own scientist and project slots hold them. Starting a project spends breakthrough points of its specialization. Refused before any input: facility_unknown, unknown_scientist (closest names), scientist_wrong_specialization, scientist_busy, unknown_project, project_wrong_specialization, project_busy, facility_has_project, scientist_required, already_assigned. Refused at the screen without starting: scientist_not_offered, project_not_offered, project_not_startable. Stable request_id; every request ends in a terminal receipt (action_unconfirmed: the effect was not observed and the request is closed; read the state again before sending a fresh one).

hoi4_special_project_recruit.description: Recruit one scientist the Recruit Scientist window offers (names under recruitable.candidates of hoi4_special_projects) for political power (25/50/75/100 by how many scientists are idle). Scientists button, Recruit Scientist, the candidate's row. Verified when the character appears in the own scientist list. Refused before any input: unknown_candidate (lists who is offered), already_recruited, insufficient_political_power.

hoi4_special_project_stop.description: Stop the running project of one own facility: facility window, the stop button and the game's 'Stop project' confirmation (accepted). Stopping takes about 10 game days (the scientist stays); canceling before an iteration completes refunds the breakthrough points once stopped. Verified when the project enters its stopping state (hoi4_special_projects shows stopping_days) or the facility shows no project. Refused before any input: facility_unknown, no_project, already_stopping.

hoi4_special_project_unassign.description: Take the scientist out of an own facility (the small button on the portrait of the facility card). Refused before any input: facility_unknown, no_scientist, facility_has_project (stop the project first with hoi4_special_project_stop and wait for it to finish stopping). Verified when the facility's scientist slot is empty.

hoi4_special_projects.description: Own special-project state read from memory (no input, no lease, nothing paused): facilities (facility_id, building, specialization, assigned scientist, running project), scientists (name, skills per specialization nuclear/naval/air/land, traits, assigned_facility_id), the visible project pool (key, specialization, base_days, running_in_facility_id) and the four breakthrough accounts (points and progress percent). Specialization 'nuclear' is called Physics on screen. A new facility is built with hoi4_construction_add (building land_facility, air_facility, naval_facility or nuclear_facility). Pass rules:true to add each project's vanilla rules from the install (breakthrough cost, parent projects, required technologies, the available trigger, prototype resources, time and complexity). Use hoi4_special_projects_panel for state names and what can be started.

hoi4_special_projects_panel.description: Open the Research panel's Experimental Facilities tab with ordinary input (W, the tab), read what only the screen shows and close the panel again: each facility card's state name, research speed, scientist and project text; with facility_id also that facility's project window: every project the game offers there now with display name, type, approximate time, requirement text ('Requires a Scientist to start') and speed. Starts nothing. Needs the lease; moves the cursor.

hoi4_state_slots.description: Free shared building slots of own states (unlocked, used, queued, free) from one memory read, no interface input; up to 12 states per call. For many states use hoi4_states with the own tag and min_free_slots / sort free_slots instead. view:true opens each state's view (Find view, one click) and reads the slot text the game shows: slow, only to check a doubtful count.

hoi4_state_snapshot.description: Everything the pure reads can see, in one call: the bodies of every read tool that takes no lease (overview, country status, economy and its detail, resources, production lines and shortages, stockpile, construction queue, research bonuses, doctrines, commanders, armies with their orders, supply per division, province and state, wars, war statistics, diplomacy, air wings and regions, fleets, convoys, occupation, intelligence, MIOs, special projects, division templates, the game's alert row, open events, completed focuses and the watcher's brief with its open omissions), each under reads.<key> with its read time in read_ms.<key>; a read that fails answers {error} in its place. `since` is passed to the watcher (hoi4_observe) so its typed changes since that sequence come too; `skip` leaves keys out. The state recorder takes one per game week. Pure read: no lease, no input, no panel, never pauses.

hoi4_states.description: States in one memory read (no interface input). A country tag (e.g. SOV, GER) lists every state it owns or controls: owner, controller, category, live building levels (buildings, factories), for the own country the shared building slots (unlocked, used, queued, free), resources, victory points with who holds them, the factories history/states gives (factories_start, an estimate for another country) and totals. Filter and sort in the same call instead of opening states one by one: owned_only, ids, min_free_slots, building with min_level/max_level, resource; sort by free_slots (default), factories, infrastructure, victory_points, level (of building), resource, id or name; limit (default 200) and offset. Large countries are read as fast as small ones: choose the few states to act on from this table, then act. A name (accent-insensitive substring) or one exact ID finds states by name instead. Pure read.

hoi4_stockpile.description: Own equipment stockpile from game memory (no input, no lease, never pauses). Per archetype (infantry_equipment, support_equipment, artillery_equipment, motorized_equipment = trucks, light_tank_chassis, ...): stockpile (pieces in storage), variants (each design in storage: type key, design_id, amount), produced_per_day (what the own production lines put out on the last daily tick, with the lines and factories behind it), fielded_need / fielded_have / fielded_short (what the own divisions need, hold and still lack: the stockpile is drawn into them first), cover_after_shortfall (stockpile minus what the divisions lack; negative = the stockpile cannot even fill them), net_per_day (the change of the stockpile per game day measured by this server over up to 30 game days; null until it has seen two game days), consumption_per_day (produced minus net), days_of_cover (stockpile / daily loss; 0 when the divisions already lack more than is stored) with depleting (false = the stock is not falling, days_of_cover null). `equipment` limits the answer to archetypes or variant type keys (a string or a list). Stockpile amounts were checked against the history files that create them; the trend needs the game to run.

hoi4_supply.description: Own divisions, the provinces and states they stand in and the supply system, read from game memory (no input, no lease, no pause). Per division: id (as hoi4_armies), army, template, state_id/province_id, hit points and percent of the template maximum, manpower against need, equipment held against need per archetype, plus supply: supply_percent (the 'Supply status' of the army tooltip, 100 = fully supplied), supply_need and supply_received per day, supply_band (full|ok|low|very_low) and the supply and demand of its province. `provinces` lists each province where own divisions stand: supply the province receives, demand placed by the units there, headroom (negative = overdrawn, the divisions there lose supply), flows from the supply nodes (node id, node province and kind when the node is own), supply hub present, railway level and naval base level. `states` gives the state's local supply and infrastructure. `supply_nodes` lists own hubs and ports with province, railway and naval base level. `below_70`/`below_50` list divisions under those supply percentages, `shortages` those with missing equipment or below `strength_below` (default 0.7) hit points, `overdrawn_provinces` the stacks that draw more than the province receives (spread them out, or build a hub or rail). Supply fields are validated:false (internally consistent, not yet compared with an on-screen reading); hub and rail throughput, trucks and trains, stored buffer and attrition are listed under `unavailable` as null. A read that catches the game rebuilding its supply map (every reached province at zero for a moment) carries no supply figures: `supply_available` false with `supply_error.code` supply_settling; read again.

summary.description: per-army rows, totals and the first 10 of each short list; no division rows (a few KB)

hoi4_technology_list.description: Canonical loaded public technology IDs with bounded filtering/pagination. Catalog membership does not imply player research eligibility; available:true lists only techs not yet researched whose prerequisites are all researched. Pure reads; never pauses.

hoi4_template_create.description: Create a new own division template with ordinary input (U panel, Division Designer button, Create Empty, battalion slots, name box, Save). `regiments` is up to 5 columns of up to 5 battalion keys from common/units (infantry, mountaineers, cavalry, motorized, artillery_brigade, anti_tank_brigade, light_armor, ...; one list per column, top to bottom, no gaps); `support` is up to 5 company keys (engineer, recon, artillery, logistics_company, ...). Saving spends army experience (5 per battalion, 10 per company, 25 per extra column on this build; the cost is read from the window and returned). Refused before any input: name_taken, name_not_typable, unit_unknown, unit_wrong_slot (a company in a column or a battalion in support), column_mixed_groups (one column holds one group: infantry/mountaineers together, cavalry or artillery in their own column), template_too_wide (> 40), regiments_gap, support_duplicate, empty_template, insufficient_experience (checked before Save). unit_not_unlocked and slot_locked are found while building (nothing is saved; the draft is dropped). Returns the receipt and the resulting hoi4_template_get row (width, hit points, organisation, manpower, equipment need, ...). `regimental_support` (the regimental support row, one company per column) is not yet built: refused with not_yet_built.

hoi4_template_delete.description: Delete an own division template (its Delete button in the U panel and the game's confirmation). The game refuses a template used by divisions (also as garrison template) or by training lines; that is reported as template_in_use (with the division and line counts) before any click. Verified when the template is gone from the own list.

hoi4_template_edit.description: Edit an own division template in place through its Edit button: give the complete new `regiments` and/or `support` layout (omitted = unchanged), `priority` (reserve, regular, elite) and/or `new_name`. Only the differing slots are touched (Shift+click removes, slot click plus a choice replaces or adds). Verified from the designer's working copy and from the saved template. Templates used by divisions or training lines are refused (template_in_use) for layout changes unless allow_in_use is true: the game then reorganises those divisions at the new composition. Same refusals as hoi4_template_create plus template_unknown, nothing_to_change. `regimental_support` (the regimental support row, one company per column) is not yet built: refused with not_yet_built.

hoi4_template_get.description: Own division templates read from game memory (no input, no lease, no pause): per template the regiment columns (column x rows, e.g. [[infantry,infantry,infantry],...]), support companies, width, hit points, base organisation (mean of the battalions and companies; `organisation_live` is the same mean times the country's organisation modifier, taken from a live division of the template), manpower, supply use, equipment need per archetype (pieces), and per equipment archetype the variant a live division holds with its per-piece stats. `equipment_stats_estimate` (soft/hard attack, defence, breakthrough, armour, piercing, air attack) is an ESTIMATE summed from each battalion's main equipment variant, validated:false. Exact fields were recomputed against common/units and live divisions (hit points and manpower matched all own divisions). Optional `template` (exact name) narrows to one.

hoi4_template_options.description: Battalion and company types the Division Designer offers now (unlocked), read from its selection window (opens the designer on an empty draft and closes it again; nothing is saved and no experience is spent): per type the key, game name, group, army experience to add, width, hit points, organisation, manpower, supply use and equipment need from the definitions. Also the extra experience for a new column per group and the army experience held.

hoi4_template_rename.description: Rename an own division template (designer name box, Update). Refused with name_taken, name_not_typable or template_unknown before input. Divisions keep using the template.

hoi4_time.description: Set desired pause or internal speed 0..4 (the game's speeds 1 to 5: 2 is the game's speed 3) with ordinary keys (Space, keypad +/-) sent only while the owned game window is front-most, each verified by fresh memory readback. Supply exactly one target and a stable request_id; uncertain dispatches are never replayed.

hoi4_trade.description: Read the Trade view (opens it with the R key, changes nothing): the player's civilian factories and, for the seven resources (oil, aluminium, rubber, tungsten, steel, chromium, coal), balance, produced, imported, exported, special projects, production lines and needed; with `resource` it also selects that resource's filter and lists its trade partners (country, units bought now, units available as 'current/available', convoys used). Selecting a filter is an ordinary click on the view. Set a purchase with hoi4_trade_set.

hoi4_trade_set.description: Buy `amount` units of `resource` from partner `country` (exact name as hoi4_trade lists it, or its three-letter tag such as USA) through the Trade view: select the resource filter, click the partner's row, set the offer window's buy slider (a click on its track, then its arrows until the window's own 'Buy amount' reads the number) and press Send. amount: an integer (0 cancels the purchase), "max" or "needed" (the window's button that buys what the country needs). Typed refusals before anything is sent: partner_not_listed (lists the partners), amount_above_available (the window's maximum is named), trade_unavailable (the game offers no slider). Verified from the partner's contracted units in the view's Delivered column after Send (the game moves the goods with convoys over the following days; imports show in the balance table once they arrive).

hoi4_train.description: Queue `count` divisions of an own template in ONE training queue with ordinary input: the template's Train button creates the queue, its + sets each line to train one division (the game's default is infinite: a line that trains forever), then Add Unit adds the other lines in parallel; the queue gets the own state deploy_state_id as location (a queue without a location never deploys). Each step is verified on the queue in memory (amount, line count).

hoi4_ui_act.description: One ordinary input on a widget by its id from hoi4_ui_inspect, then what changed: `changed` (windows opened or closed, widgets shown, hidden, enabled, disabled, new text) and `state_changed` (political power, stability, war support, manpower, factories, resources, alerts with their deltas). Refused before any input: widget_not_found / widget_ambiguous (with candidates), widget_forbidden (console and debug controls), widget_hidden, widget_disabled, widget_without_rectangle; irreversible_needs_confirmation when the files say the click spends something or cannot be undone (pass confirm_irreversible:true only when you mean it); dialog_needs_answer_flag for a pop-up's buttons (answer_dialog:true). action: click (default), right_click, shift_click, ctrl_click, hover (rest the cursor on it), scroll_up, scroll_down; times repeats a click (1-10). When it worked, keep it with hoi4_skill_save. Example: {"widget": "topbar/decisionview_button", "action": "click", "request_id": "r1", "lease_token": "..."}

wait_ms.description: how long to wait before reading what changed

widget.description: widget id from hoi4_ui_inspect (or a name only one shown widget has)

hoi4_ui_inspect.description: Read-only: every open window and its widgets from the game's interface memory, for panels no other tool knows (a mod's own mechanics, a new DLC). Each widget has a stable `id` (the path of .gui element names, e.g. "topbar/decisionview_button"; `#n` numbers repeated names, `#n` below a grid numbers its entries), `kind` (button, icon, text, container, grid, ...), `at` [x,y,w,h] on screen when known, `enabled:false` when the game greys it out, `text` for text boxes, and `script`: what the game's and the mod's interface files say (tooltip text, the scripted effect a mod's button runs, what it spends, what cannot be undone). Pass `window` (a window id or a widget id) to read one panel; `all:true` adds hidden widgets. No input, no lease, never pauses. Example: {"window": "topbar"}

hidden_windows.description: also list windows the game keeps hidden (default false)

window.description: a window id from an earlier reading, or a widget id to read only that subtree

hoi4_volunteers.description: Send or recall volunteer divisions, or send an attache, by the diplomacy view's own actions through the in-process module (family volunteers; HOI4_BACKEND=inprocess until S24-VOLUNTEERS passes). The game's own legality decides (the volunteer cap from the defines, the divisions-required floor, the recall lock, war and ideology gates); a refusal posts nothing. Divisions: an army's divisions, or division_ids within it. Air volunteers are a rebase of wings to an air base of the receiver (hoi4_air_rebase), not this tool.

army.description: send / recall: the army whose divisions go (all of them unless division_ids)

country.description: the receiving country's tag (the country at war; for recall the country the volunteers serve in)

hoi4_wait_change.description: Block until a change after `since` arrives (optionally only given kinds or urgent ones), or until timeout_seconds (1-30) pass; then reply like hoi4_observe with woke_because change|timeout. `now.omissions` lists what the game marks actionable and is still open (item, days_open, the game's todo, the executor rule that owns it, that rule's dated note, note_contradicts_read), longest open first, so a wake needs no alert read. Use it instead of polling: the reply comes within a few hundred milliseconds of the change. Pure read; never pauses.

hoi4_wait_for.description: Bounded server wait for own focus/research change, game date, research UI, or all explicit until_assignments targets. Assignment targets check the first sample too and mean active focus/current slot assignment, not completion over game time or a durable plan receipt. Choose one target family. Date/assignment waits pin the current owned worker and wake on its terminal disposition or owner retirement; lifecycle evidence is historical and proves no completion. A wait begun without a worker does not attach to a later plan. UI/assignment matches do not authorize input. Wall timeout returns only an explicitly historical earlier accepted sample; no late target is accepted. Never pauses.

hoi4_war_goal_targets.description: Which enemy-owned states to demand in the peace conference, ranked by points, industry, manpower and resources with tiers (must_take, worth_taking, optional), resource prizes, contiguous blocks, own cores and which states we already occupy. A read, not an action; the conference cost itself is not modelled. No lease.

hoi4_war_risk.description: Read-only, before justifying or declaring war on `country`: which countries would join that war on its side (its faction, every country guaranteeing it, its overlord and subjects) and which of our borders with them are not held (need a division in every border state and two per state). hoi4_diplomacy_act declare_war refuses with war_would_widen in that case unless accept_widening:true. Memory and map files only; no input.

hoi4_war_stats.description: Read-only (memory, no input, no pause): casualties per country in each war, as the war overview counts them. Each war is a group of war relations (sides inferred by who fights whom); per relation the losses of both countries (men), per war the sum per side, and per country the game's own total (the `casualties` trigger formula: sum over its wars plus the largest extra count). By default only the wars the player fights; all:true lists every war in the world. War score, leaders and goals are not read here (see hoi4_diplomacy_state).

hoi4_wars.description: Own land borders, occupied and threatened own states, from state owner/controller, own division positions and state adjacency derived from the install map files. Pure read; no lease. Stage B: wars lists the own wars (enemies, allies at war, start date) from war relations; sides, leaders, war score and justification timers are unvalidated; surrender progress (wars[].enemy_surrender_progress, own_surrender_progress) and the naval intel against each enemy (wars[].own_naval_intel) are not yet built and always null with a reason; hostility is the war enemies plus the occupation proxy and the optional enemies tags you pass; covered is a heuristic (own divisions stand in the border states), not a front-line-order read. Alerts: own_state_occupied, border_uncovered, threatened_state_undefended. capital_land: own-controlled states the capital reaches over own-controlled land (history capital, else the largest own area); a division elsewhere is overseas (disbanding it loses 75% of its equipment).
